faq_items.question: What is retro wall art?
faq_items.answer: Retro wall art borrows the look of roughly the 1950s through 1970s: simplified suns and rainbows, abstract organic curves, checkerboard, and warm earthy tones like mustard, rust, avocado, and terracotta. It reads as playful and nostalgic, and it pairs naturally with mid-century furniture, thrifted finds, and houseplants.

faq_items.question: Where can I get free retro wall art to print?
faq_items.answer: Download a free printable retro art PDF built at full letter size and 300 DPI, like the mid-century sun design in this post. Printables skip shipping, arrive instantly, and cost only paper and ink, so you can test a look on your wall before committing to anything framed.

faq_items.question: What paper should I use to print retro wall art?
faq_items.answer: Use 32 lb matte presentation paper or a smooth cardstock rather than thin copy paper. Heavier matte stock holds bold retro colors, resists ink bleed, and feels substantial in a frame, so a home print looks bought instead of homemade. Print at your printer's highest quality setting.

faq_items.question: How do I print wall art at the right size?
faq_items.answer: Open the PDF and choose "actual size" or set the scale to 100 percent, never "fit to page," which shrinks the image and leaves an uneven border. Files built at 8.5 by 11 inches drop straight into standard letter-size frames with no trimming or guesswork.

faq_items.question: How high should I hang retro prints?
faq_items.answer: Hang the center of a print or arrangement at eye level, about 57 to 60 inches from the floor. Above furniture, keep the bottom of the frame six to ten inches above the sofa or bed so the two read as a pair. Removable strips make it renter-friendly.
